turns.assistant_text:
### Tình hình công ty NVIDIA hiện tại sau bê bối của CEO

1. **Bê bối của CEO Jensen Huang**:
   - CEO Jensen Huang của NVIDIA đang bị điều tra liên quan đến mối quan hệ tình cảm với một phụ nữ mà tình báo Mỹ cho rằng là gián điệp Trung Quốc. Huang đã thừa nhận có một mối quan hệ tình cảm và công ty đang tiến hành một cuộc điều tra chính thức về vấn đề này. [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/09/a-short-seller-flagged-nvidia-ceos-ties-to-a-suspected-chinese-spy-six-months-before-the-scandal) cho biết rằng mối quan hệ này đã bị một công ty bán khống nêu ra từ sáu tháng trước.

2. **Phản ứng từ Trung Quốc**:
   - Bộ Ngoại giao Trung Quốc đã bác bỏ các báo cáo về việc nước này cử gián điệp để tiếp cận Huang, gọi đó là một chiến dịch bôi nhọ. [Washington Post](https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2026/11/09/china-dismisses-reports-plot-ensnare-nvidia-ceo-smear-campaign).

3. **Tình hình tài chính và đầu tư**:
   - Mặc dù có bê bối, NVIDIA vẫn được coi là một công ty mạnh mẽ với tiềm năng tăng trưởng dài hạn. Các nhà phân tích cho rằng bê bối này không ảnh hưởng đến tăng trưởng doanh thu của công ty. [The Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/09/huang-s-actions-prompt-nvidia-board-to-launch-investigation-here-s-what-investors-need-to-know) đã chỉ ra rằng công ty không phải là một "show diễn của một người" mà có nhiều nhân viên chủ chốt khác.

4. **Cuộc điều tra nội bộ**:
   - NVIDIA đã mở một cuộc điều tra để xem xét liệu Huang có thực sự là mục tiêu của một nỗ lực tình báo nước ngoài hay không. Công ty khẳng định không có lý do nào để tin rằng an ninh quốc gia hoặc bí mật của NVIDIA đã bị xâm phạm. [PBS News](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/nvidia-investigates-whether-ceo-jensen-huang-was-targeted-by-chinese-spy-when-he-had-affair).

5. **Tác động đến cổ phiếu**:
   - Cổ phiếu của NVIDIA đã giảm do những tin tức tiêu cực liên quan đến CEO, nhưng các nhà phân tích cho rằng đây có thể là cơ hội mua vào cho các nhà đầu tư. [Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4965015-nvidia-allegation-driven-dip-creates-a-buying-opportunity).

Tình hình hiện tại của NVIDIA đang rất phức tạp với nhiều yếu tố ảnh hưởng từ bê bối cá nhân của CEO, nhưng công ty vẫn giữ vững vị thế trên thị trường.

items.title: A short seller flagged Nvidia CEO's ties to a suspected Chinese spy six months before the scandal | TechCrunch
items.summary:
Six months before the Nvidia spy scandal emerged, the New York-based short seller firm Culper Research had already raised questions about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s unusually close relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that buys Nvidia chips. She is now suspected to be a Chinese spy. [...] The Nvidia CEO admitted to an extramarital affair over the weekend, and the company has now opened a formal investigation into his relationship with Alice Huang (who shares his last name but is not related). U.S. intelligence officials believe she was recruited by the Chinese government to collect intelligence on Jensen Huang and influence his position regarding U.S. export controls on advanced AI chips. [...] Culper’s May 13 report is resurfacing because it picked up on the connection between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang while investigating Megaspeed’s ties to Nvidia.

In particular, the report called the relationship between the two executives “uncomfortably close,” noting that the Nvidia CEO was spotted partying and socializing with Alice Huang on multiple occasions. The report even claimed that some Nvidia employees wondered whether they had a “special relationship.”

items.title: Alice Huang and Nvidia; what we know about Jensen Huang spy scandal | CNN
items.summary:
CNN’s Kevin Liptak looks at President Trump and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s close ties over the years as Huang reels from the fallout of admitting to having an extramarital affair and his company announced it would investigate reports that he was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.”

The New York Times also reported that intelligence officials were conducting electronic surveillance of Alice Huang for at least a year, and had briefed President Donald Trump on the matter last year. [...] She’s been photographed with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (no relation) at banquet dinners and golf resorts, clinking wine glasses and even leaving an event with him in the same car.

But for someone suddenly generating international headlines, she remains something of a mystery.

Her limited online footprint paints a picture of a journalist-turned tech power broker who held senior positions at financial firms in Asia. [...] Trump said he did not regret not taking action, and downplayed Jensen Huang’s culpability in the incident on Monday. He said he believed that the Nvidia CEO was unaware of any potential motivations of espionage.

On Monday, China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs called the allegations that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy “groundless speculation and an attempt to smear and malign China.”

CNN’s Isaac Yee and Wayne Chang contributed to this report from Taipei.

items.title: WATCH: Trump says FBI is looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese agent | PBS News
items.summary:
# WATCH: Trump says FBI is looking into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese agent

WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump said Monday that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang should not worry about the FBI looking into his affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese government agent.

President Donald Trump responded to spy plot allegations involving Nvidia's CEO in a White House briefing Monday. Watch his remarks in the player above. [...] Huang has acknowledged he had been intimate with a business executive, issuing an apology to his wife and to the company in an open letter posted on Nvidia's website. He did not name the woman.

Nvidia announced Sunday it was conducting an independent investigation into reports that Huang was the "target of a foreign intelligence effort."

The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence determined that the woman was gathering information for Beijing. [...] The New York Times said Alice Huang was a former executive of a Singapore-based data center company called Megaspeed International, whose website prominently touts its partnership with Nvidia.

Many offices in Singapore were closed on Monday for a holiday. Megaspeed and the Singapore Ministry of Home Affairs did not immediately reply to requests for comment.

items.title: Nvidia built itself around one man. A scandal is testing that bet | Fortune
items.summary:
There are few other cases, if any, that resemble Nvidia’s current situation. Corporate executives whose romantic liaisons have derailed their careers are common enough. In 2019, McDonald’s fired CEO Steve Easterbrook over a consensual relationship with an employee that violated company policy. The bigger scandal came afterward: the company discovered additional undisclosed relationships, sued to recover his exit compensation, and ultimately recovered cash and equity valued at $105 million. In [...] “The board has made a mistake by not having a clearly outlined succession plan that’s been telegraphed to the market for a year or two,” Schloetzer said. “They find themselves at the day of reckoning, and it’s a sudden and perhaps forced one, rather than a relay situation where they have time to figure it out as they go.” [...] The board could oust Huang at the end of its investigation, or Huang could have to step down before then, Burke said. He could also leave the CEO role but stay on in another capacity.

In media interviews over the years, Huang has dismissed conventional succession planning, saying his approach is to continually transfer his knowledge to colleagues. He has also said he hopes Nvidia’s next CEO already works at the company, even though Nvidia has not publicly identified a successor.

items.title: Huang’s Actions Prompt Nvidia Board to Launch Investigation. Here’s What Investors Need to Know. | The Motley Fool
items.summary:
What may be the biggest concern here is the idea that Nvidia's successes are often seen as linked to one person: Jensen Huang. The company hasn't revealed an official succession plan if Huang were to ever step down for any reason. Though Huang isn't about to leave right now, the current situation may stir up concern among investors and weigh on the stock. [...] It's important to keep in mind, however, that though Jensen Huang is a visionary driving Nvidia, he works closely with 60 direct staff members who all share information. So Nvidia isn't exactly a one-person show. Today, in light of the current uncertainty, investors shouldn't panic and instead should remain focused on the elements that truly drive Nvidia's growth, such as its innovation, current AI demand, and long-term prospects. All of those remain intact. [...] While the current investigation may signal turbulence for the stock price today and even in the months to come, the company's solid long-term story isn't broken.

items.title: Nvidia investigates whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese spy when he had affair | PBS News
items.summary:
Nvidia is opening an investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the "target of a foreign intelligence effort," the company's board of directors said Sunday.

The announcement came after Huang acknowledged to the board that he had been intimate with a business executive whom, according to The New York Times, U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing.

READ MORE: Nvidia announced a software tool to stop rogue AI. How would it work? [...] Nvidia's board said it has "no reason to believe" that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information. Huang "fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it," the board said.

READ MORE: Taiwan charges 9 over illegal AI server exports to China, including Nvidia and Super Micro staffers

Huang, 63, will remain CEO during the investigation. [...] "I just can't comment because of the nature of it," he told reporters. "And I also can't comment on an internal corporate matter that's going on with Nvidia."

Nvidia, the world's most valuable company, has regularly surpassed Wall Street's earnings expectations in the past three years since its high-end chips emerged as AI's best building blocks. The Santa Clara, California-based company reported quarterly profits of $59.69 billion in August.

The company hasn't revealed an official succession plan if Huang were to ever step down for any reason. Though Huang isn't about to leave right now, the current situation may stir up concern among investors and weigh on the stock. [...] It's important to keep in mind, however, that though Jensen Huang is a visionary driving Nvidia, he works closely with 60 direct staff members who all share information. So Nvidia isn't exactly a one-person show. Today, in light of the current uncertainty, investors shouldn't panic and instead should remain focused on the elements that truly drive Nvidia's growth, such as its innovation, current AI demand, and long-term prospects. All of those remain intact. [...] While the current investigation may signal turbulence for the stock price today and even in the months to come, the company's solid long-term story isn't broken.

items.title: Nvidia investigates whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by Chinese spy when he had affair | PBS News
items.summary:
Nvidia is opening an investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the "target of a foreign intelligence effort," the company's board of directors said Sunday.

The announcement came after Huang acknowledged to the board that he had been intimate with a business executive whom, according to The New York Times, U.S. intelligence determined was gathering information for Beijing.

READ MORE: Nvidia announced a software tool to stop rogue AI. How would it work? [...] Nvidia's board said it has "no reason to believe" that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information. Huang "fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it," the board said.

READ MORE: Taiwan charges 9 over illegal AI server exports to China, including Nvidia and Super Micro staffers

Huang, 63, will remain CEO during the investigation. [...] "I just can't comment because of the nature of it," he told reporters. "And I also can't comment on an internal corporate matter that's going on with Nvidia."

Nvidia, the world's most valuable company, has regularly surpassed Wall Street's earnings expectations in the past three years since its high-end chips emerged as AI's best building blocks. The Santa Clara, California-based company reported quarterly profits of $59.69 billion in August.
